content.comment_body: Hello, can anyone advise how to find the IP address of a [product_name] without display? The module is pre-used and I don't have the original project. I'm running [product_name] software V8.3 and the module's article number is [article_no]. Thanks for your assistance.

Start a new network project in your engineering software. Then select 'Go Online' and let the software scan for all connected [product_name]s on your network. The detected devices will be shown there.
Hi [user_name], thanks for your quick answer. Unfortunately, this method didn't solve the issue. Is there a way to perform a 'factory reset' on this type of module?

With a [product_name] without display, factory reset can only be done via engineering software. But if the software can't find the IP address, what can you do? What are your PC's IP address and subnet mask? Was the device brand new? We'll need more details.
My PC's IP is 192.168.28.11 and subnet mask is 255.255.255.0. The [product_name] was programmed before. Also, the status LED is red (STOP).
The device might have an IP address outside your network range. Did you acquire the [product_name] from online marketplaces? This might be causing the issue.
It looks like the [product_name] isn't set up in the same subnet as your PC.
I received this [product_name] for free, so it's disappointing if I can't get it working.

Here's something to try: Create a simple program (e.g., I1 to Q1). In the file settings, assign the IP address and subnet mask to match your PC's network. Save it as a .bin file on an mSD card. Then insert the card into your [product_name] and restart it with the power supply.
Another issue: The module with your article number could be one of several versions. If you need, I can provide .bin files for both possibilities.
A red LED may mean the [product_name] doesn't have a valid program. Attached are the two .bin files; try each one in sequence.
Thank you, it's working again! Your help was invaluable.
Glad to hear it's up and running.

I expect there will be more questions ahead. I'm interested in connecting an HMI device to the [product_name] and, as a self-taught user, I hope it's okay to keep asking for advice. Also, excuse my English; I rely on a translator since I'm Czech and speak only Czech.
That’s perfectly fine. If anyone needs clarification, they'll ask. You're welcome to post as many questions as you need, and the community will do its best to support you.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is struggling to identify or reset the IP address of a used [product_name] module that lacks a display and is missing the original project files. Efforts to use [product_name] programming software (V8.3) for network scanning are unsuccessful, likely due to mismatched subnet configurations. The core issue is difficulty in recovering or resetting the hardware acquired second-hand and not having straightforward access to required settings.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for an easy method to discover or reset the IP address of the [product_name] module, ideally without needing a display or original project files.
